subject: 2026 MLB MVP
title: Who won MVP 2026? Yordan Alvarez and Pete Crow-Armstrong, unanimously
answer: Houston's Yordan Alvarez won the 2026 American League MVP and the Chicago Cubs' Pete Crow-Armstrong won the National League MVP, both unanimously, the Baseball Writers' Association of America announced Thursday, Nov. 12, 2026. Each received all 30 first-place votes.
in_the_news: It was only the third time both MVP votes were unanimous, and 2026 became the first season in which both MVPs and both Cy Young winners were unanimous picks.
body:
Alvarez, 29, won the AL batting title at .316 with 42 home runs, 106 RBIs, a major league-best 109 walks and a .432 on-base percentage. He played 158 games after being limited to 48 in 2025 by a wrist fracture and an ankle sprain, and he was named AL Comeback Player of the Year a day earlier. He is the third Astros MVP, after Jeff Bagwell (1994) and Jose Altuve (2017). Tampa Bay's Junior Caminero finished second and Kansas City's Bobby Witt Jr. third.

Crow-Armstrong, 24, hit .280 with 45 homers and 41 stolen bases and led the majors with 10.6 fWAR, while also winning a Gold Glove and the Platinum Glove in center field. He walked 83 times after drawing just 29 walks the year before. He is the Cubs' 13th MVP and their first since Kris Bryant in 2016. Shohei Ohtani finished second and Milwaukee's Brice Turang third.

The MVP announcement closed MLB awards week. Earlier, the Yankees' Cam Schlittler and the Brewers' Jacob Misiorowski won the Cy Young Awards, also unanimously. Both MVP votes were cast by 30 BBWAA writers before the postseason began.

faq.a: Yordan Alvarez of the Houston Astros, unanimously.
Pete Crow-Armstrong of the Chicago Cubs, unanimously. Shohei Ohtani was runner-up.

faq.q: How many times have both MVPs been unanimous?

faq.a: Thirty members of the Baseball Writers' Association of America, two per league city, vote at the end of the regular season.
